text: Investigating the `Interval.fromISO` / `Settings.throwOnInvalid` bug in `src/interval.js` now. Estimated fix ready in ~8 minutes.

`parseDigits` returns `NaN` when the input string contains no parseable digits.

In `src/impl/digits.js`, `parseInt(str, 10)` is `NaN` for such input, so the fallback branch runs: `value` starts as `""`, the loop appends nothing for non-digit characters, and the final `parseInt("", 10)` yields `NaN`. So `parseDigits("")`, `parseDigits("abc")` → `NaN` (not `0`/`undefined`/`null`).

Bug: `Interval.fromISO` in `src/interval.js` called `DateTime.fromISO(s, opts)` / `DateTime.fromISO(e, opts)` unguarded, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` a valid `<datetime>/<duration>` (or `<duration>/<datetime>`) interval threw while the duration half was being parsed as a DateTime, instead of falling through to the `Duration.fromISO` branch.

Fix: wrapped each `DateTime.fromISO` call in try/catch and branched on `startIsValid` / `endIsValid`.

Checks: `npx jest test/interval` → 127/127 pass; ad-hoc tests confirm that with `throwOnInvalid = true`, `Interval.fromISO('2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M')` and `'P1Y2M10DT2H30M/2008-05-11T15:30:00'` return valid Intervals (they threw before the fix), `'nonsense'` throws, and with `throwOnInvalid = false` `'nonsense'` returns `isValid === false` / `invalidReason === 'unparsable'`. eslint clean; no other files touched.

Fixed and verified.

Bug in `src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js`: the constructor stored the raw argument (`this.fixed = offset`) with no numeric validation, and `get isValid()` was hard-coded to `return true`. So a zone built from a non-numeric offset reported itself valid.

Fix: `this.fixed = isNumber(offset) ? offset : NaN;` and `get isValid() { return isNumber(this.fixed) && !Number.isNaN(this.fixed); }`. No change needed in `datetime.js` — it already propagates invalid zones (`unsupportedZone`).

Checks: `new FixedOffsetZone(undefined/null/'bogus'/NaN/{}).isValid === false` (was `true` before), `new FixedOffsetZone(0/60).isValid === true`, `utcInstance.isValid === true`, and `DateTime.fromMillis(0, {zone: new FixedOffsetZone(undefined)}).isValid === false` while the UTC-zone DateTime is valid. `npx jest test/zones` → 32/32 pass; full suite unchanged (only the 2 known pre-existing French-locale `toFormat` failures). eslint clean.

Exactly three values: `'narrow'`, `'short'`, and `'techie'` — anything else throws `RangeError: Value format <x> is out of range for property format`.

The abstract `Zone#formatOffset` in `src/zone.js` documents them, and the real implementation is `formatOffset(offset, format)` in `src/impl/util.js`:

- `'narrow'` → `±H` if minutes are 0, else `±H:MM` (minutes not zero-padded), e.g. `-5:30`, `+0`
- `'short'` → `±HH:MM`, e.g. `-05:30`, `+00:00`
- `'techie'` → `±HHMM`, e.g. `-0530`, `+0000`

Subclasses (`FixedOffsetZone`, `IANAZone`, `LocalZone`) delegate to it; `InvalidZone` overrides it to return `""`. (`offsetName(ts, {format})` is a different method and takes `'long'`/`'short'`.)

Fixed and verified.

Bug in `src/duration.js`: three missing entries in the unit-conversion matrices, so `matrix[toUnit][fromUnit]` was `undefined` and conversions produced `NaN`/`0`:
- `casualMatrix.years` was missing `quarters: 4`
- `casualMatrix.quarters` was missing `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60`
- `accurateMatrix.years` was missing `quarters: 4`

Checks: an 81-pair sweep over all unit pairs now passes for both `casual` and `longterm` accuracy (before: 4 bad pairs casual, 2 bad longterm, e.g. `{quarters:1}.as('seconds')` gave `0` instead of `7862400`); `Duration.fromObject({years:1, quarters:1}).normalize()` no longer yields `NaN`. `npx jest test/duration` → 114/114 pass; full suite unchanged (only the 2 known pre-existing French-locale `toFormat` failures). eslint clean.

Fixed and verified.

Bug in `src/impl/util.js`, `objToLocalTS`: for years 0–99 it built a 19XX date and reverted the century with `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, keeping the 19XX month/day. Because 2000 is a leap year and 100 is not, every date at/after 0100-03-01 came out one day early (e.g. `0099-12-31`.plus({days:61}) → `0100-03-01` instead of `0100-03-02`).

Fix: `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)`.

Checks: an exhaustive sweep of `plus({days:1..400})` from 6 start days across years 0–105 (and `plus({months:1..36})`) against an independent proleptic-Gregorian reference → 0 mismatches after the fix (2142 before); `npx jest test/datetime/math.test.js` → 47/47 pass; full suite unchanged (only the 2 known pre-existing French-locale `toFormat` failures). eslint/prettier clean.

Fixed and verified.

Bug in `src/impl/util.js`, `padStart`: `("0".repeat(n) + input).slice(-n)` dropped the minus sign, so negative years were mis-padded (`toISODate()` for year -1 gave `00-1-01-01`).

Fix: sign-aware padding — `padded = "-" + ("" + -input).padStart(n, "0")` for negatives, `("" + input).padStart(n, "0")` otherwise.

Checks: `toISODate()` now gives `-0001-01-01`, `-0012-01-01`, `-0100-01-01`, `-1234-01-01`, and unchanged `0005-01-01` / `2020-01-01`. `npx jest test/datetime` → 553 passed, only the 2 known pre-existing French-locale `toFormat` failures. eslint clean.

Hour 24 is valid only when it is exactly the end-of-day 24:00:00.000:

```js
const validHour =
  integerBetween(hour, 0, 23) ||
  (hour === 24 && minute === 0 && second === 0 && millisecond === 0);
```

So `hour === 24` is allowed iff `minute`, `second`, and `millisecond` are all strictly `=== 0` (not `undefined`/`"0"`). Anything else (e.g. `24:00:00.001`, `24:01`) fails with "unit out of range". `24:00` is then normalized to the next day's 00:00 by `objToLocalTS`/`Date.UTC`.
